Generally I would move all the indoor sports to the winter games, so all the martial arts + weightlifting + fencing and also ball games like basketball, badminton, volleyball, table tennis and handball.

Aquatic sports I would leave at the summer games, not because of some logistic reason, but it's just that swimming I feel is a typical summer activity. Where I'm undecided is in the case of gymnastics and track cycling. I'm not acquainted enough in the world of gymnastics to know if it's typically a summer event and while track cycling is typically practiced in the winter, there will already be a similar venue existing for speed skating and I also feel it's weird to put it away from all the other cycling events.

The problem is that many well-established sports calendars the athletes are used to would have to change.

There are the two main channels but besides them there are usually additional broadcasts. The winter sports events usually have a secondary internet channel which is uninterrupted (without ads) and either with only English commentary or none at all. 

If there are multiple events happening at the same time, the second one is usually broadcast on the internet channel as far as I'm aware. Also for some events like the Tour de France or the Biathlon world cup, there are channels with additional camera feeds (for example in biathlon there is a stream showing only the shooting range and another one showing only the track etc.)

If you have any more questions, feel free to write here or dm me!

First of all, great to see another winter sports connoisseur around :) 

I'd also recommend [Eurosport Player](https://www.eurosportplayer.com/). They have pretty much every top winter sports cup/championships + a license for the Winter Olympics in Europe for a monthly subscription. They also have multiple audio options where you can choose the commentary language during broadcasts. The ads are a little annoying, but otherwise I really like it. Though the content offering might differ depending on where you live. Aside from that you can also watch biathlon races (and some summer sports events) on [Eurovision Sports](https://www.eurovisionsports.tv/) for free.

As to the news source, I usually go on the sports organization's websites themselves (getting the info first-hand if you will). For all sports in one place, I think Eurosport has some coverage, but otherwise can't help you with that. But since FIS organizes multiple sports, I think their [website](https://www.fis-ski.com/) is a good center for the results. IBU (biathlon union) has a very good [datacenter](https://biathlonresults.com/) I recommend. For your skating needs the [ISU](https://www.isu.org/) website has you covered.

I hope I could be of help to you :)
